headlines.text: What we know about stabbing on Flydubai flight to Israel. The captain and first officer were injured, and one pilot has been arrested, officials say.

Six smugglers jailed for manslaughter over worst Channel small boats disaster. Thirty-one migrants died when their boat went down in November 2021. The trial found that the guilty men were part of two smuggling networks.
UK-France 'one in, one out' migrant scheme scrapped. Some 1,500 people have been removed to France since the scheme began just over a year ago.
Execution of US murderer Christa Pike halted shortly before it was due to happen. Pike was convicted and sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer.

Russia launches largest attack on Ukraine energy infrastructure since spring. In total 11 regions of the country were attacked overnight, with residential buildings and railways also targeted, the Ukrainian PM says.
Last UK and US troops leave Iraq as anti-Islamic State mission ends. The withdrawal of coalition forces, under a deal agreed two years ago, was a key demand of the Iraqi government.
Ethiopia fighting escalates in Tigray killing 52 civilians, medic tells the BBC. The deadly fighting has also spread to neighbouring regions, stranding tourists in Lalibela.
Girl has multiple surgeries to control infections after strike in Gaza. Witnesses say Raseel's tent was hit by an Israeli helicopter strike. Israel’s military says it has no record of the attack.
US actor Chad Lowe 'heartbroken' by death of daughter Fiona aged 13. Lowe and his wife Kim Painter announce the death of their daughter, who "was the light of our lives".
Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons. Mindgard said it discovered in July that Kimi models K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade developer's safety limits.
Singapore launches matchmaking service for government workers. The launch of FirstDate comes as the ageing nation wrestles with a record-low fertility rate.
Africa's richest man launches Kenya oil refinery despite land protests. The Kenya refinery is part of Dangote's ambitious bid to expand and help industralise Africa by 2030.
'He will never walk free': Indian judge's letter promises child sex abuse survivor. In the emotional letter, the judge describes the survivor as "the bravest little girl this court has ever seen".
Botswana condemned for slaughtering 23 elephants for independence celebrations. The government authorises the hunting of elephants and dozens of other wild animals for independence day feasts.
Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after more than 100 allege brain injuries. Hundreds of riders were allegedly injured on X2, which has seats that spin 360 degrees.
Is Spain’s anti-eviction decree a fix for its housing crisis?. The government blames 'savage speculation' as critics say new measures leave small landlords 'out in the cold'.
Why is Hegseth cutting 20 percent of US general and admiral positions?. The overhaul could reshape the US military as Hegseth faces scrutiny over senior officers’ removal.
Pep Guardiola backs Man City after guilty verdict on financial charges. The Spanish coach won 20 trophies during a glittering 10 years as City manager before departing in May.
Palestinian archaeologists race against time to save Gaza’s heritage. A Palestinian team rescued Gaza's artefacts. The question now is where to store them.
Why Israel is interfering in Palestinian education. The occupation authorities are trying to censor Palestinian school curricula because they teach national consciousness.
Christa Pike seeks firing squad, not lethal injection: Inside US executions. Women make up about 1 percent of US executions. How do states put people to death, and why is it contested?
Israeli attacks on Gaza kill seven as ‘ceasefire’ violations continue. At least six people killed in drone attack on passenger van and one person killed in strike on residential apartment.
Settlers closing in on Ramallah. Israeli settlers are encroaching ever closer to Ramallah, the de facto capital of the occupied West Bank.
Denmark vs Portugal: UEFA Nations League – Ronaldo, Hojlund, teams, form. Reigning champions Portugal look to build on their winning start as they take on Denmark on match day three.
Rainwater washes away highway in Nigeria. Heavy rain over three days caused severe flooding along the Agbarho-Ughelli highway in Delta State, southern Nigeria.
Former journalist crowned king of Uganda’s Tooro kingdom. Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, a former journalist, has been crowned the king of Uganda’s Tooro Kingdom.
How does Iraq’s security change after US forces withdraw?. Iraq marks US troop withdrawal with 'Sovereignty Days', symbolising a shift after decades of foreign military presence.
Iraq celebrates National Sovereignty Day as US troops withdraw. Iraq’s security forces held parades in Baghdad and Najaf to celebrate ‘Sovereignty Day’ as US troops withdraw.
Is Iran losing its leverage over the Strait of Hormuz?. Crude flows through Hormuz have recovered, but tanker insurance costs and geopolitical risks remain barriers to a return to normality.
Flydubai flight to Israel diverted after attack on pilot. Dramatic video shows the aftermath of an attack on a pilot on a Flydubai flight to the Israeli city of Tel Aviv.

Venezuelan national shot by ICE officer in Austin charged with assaulting federal officer. The Justice Department charged Wilber Rafael Garces-Perez with assaulting a federal officer after an Austin vehicle pursuit ended in an ICE shooting.

Cam Schlittler and Ben Rice, Yankees’ own Massachusetts natives, crush Red Sox in Game 1 blowout. Cam Schlittler struck out 10 in 6.1 scoreless innings and Ben Rice launched a grand slam as the New York Yankees routed Boston without Aaron Judge.

Chicago White Sox stun Houston Astros to take 1-0 lead in American League Wild Card Series. Hagen Smith and Colson Montgomery led the Chicago White Sox past the Houston Astros in Game 1, putting the worst-record playoff team in an early hole.

Aces' A'ja Wilson gets tech for confrontation with Fever fan, who was determined to have broken no rules. A'ja Wilson drew a technical foul after confronting a spectator in Game 2, but arena security found no fan code of conduct violation at all.

Transgender athletes have taken 2,293 championship spots from biological women, new research finds. New research found transgender athletes have taken 2,293 championship spots from biological women since the mid-1980s across more than 14,000 events.

Reparations activists call out blue states for using slavery history to fund broader agenda. U.S. Freedmen Project activists argue immigrants and non-foundational Black Americans should be excluded from reparations for slavery descendants.

Caitlin Clark's technical foul sparks furious rally as Fever avoid elimination against Aces. Caitlin Clark made WNBA playoff history with a points-assists double-double before halftime as the Indiana Fever surged past the Las Vegas Aces.

Hurricane Polo's remnants bringing more rain to flood-struck U.S. Southwest. The storm's remnants battered the U.S. Southwest, flooding roadways and forcing residents in small New Mexico towns to evacuate over concerns about a dam failing.

The federal law aimed at protecting college students from sexual abuse. The lawsuit by a former Cornell University student, alleging she was raped in 2024 by seven male students, has renewed long-standing concerns about how colleges deal with sexual assault.
